M O R E   M A I L ! !


    April, 1992      Page Reply

 How to write to us...02     -
 R. Webster...........03    07
 C. Grant Dixon.......14    17
 S. Glenn.............18    22
 Dominic Morris.......30    33
 Burkhard Taige.......38    43
 Vincent L. Jacks.....44    45
 Hermann Reichel......46    47

   PLEASE SEND YOUR TEXTFILE!
Text is accepted in any form for
OUTLETTERS: wordprocessor files
(say which),typed or handwritten
letters. However, PLEASE send us
a textfile if possible so your
letter needn't be typed again!
The easiest for us to edit are
Tasword 2 files with the right
margin set at 32 but a textfile
in ANY format is appreciated!

Please state if there should be
parts of your letter you do not
wish published but we always use
our discretion anyway. Letters
may also be edited for clarity
and length... Please ask if you
welcome direct correspondence
from other OUTLET readers and we
will publish your full address.

From: R. Webster, NSW, AUSTRALIA

Dear Sir,

I have the February 1992 FORMAT
magazine and saw your advert for
OUTLET! As I see it OUTLET is a
magazine on a disk. I could be
wrong but I'm interested. Now I
have a SPECTRUM + with the
interface and Disk from Datel
Electronics but my printer is a
TANDY/IBM DMP 106, Graphics IBM.

I have a CAD program by KEMSOFT.
This was bought as a tape prog-
ram for my other interface that
I made from the EVERYDAY
ELECTRONICS magazine by KEN
TAYLOR. With this interface I
get a printout but if I use the


+D and Disk it will not print to
my printer unless I use the
Screen$ 1 and this is not good
enough. I did write to the
KEMSOFT company about it but he
must have gone bump or he does
not want to know because I said
I can't, as a pensioner, afford
another thirty quid.

First of all I am not a program-
mer and have only the basic
knowledge of fiddling a program.
So, I need lots of help from
England as no one here is inter-
ested in Sinclair Computers -not
even AMSTRAD.

This Tasword 2 is on disk only
because I used the Snapshot and
to get it to print without

a (?) at the beginning of every
line I have found the line to
print and used the print @ 6,1.
at the begining of the line in
the program.

There is a Tasword 2 sort
program in this months magazine
of FORMAT but this will not work
with my version as I took
Tasword as a snapshot file;
that's what I think anyway. So I
need to have my Tasword 2 and
the CAD program to run as a disk
program.

Is there a Spectrum program that
I could use to draw the frame-
work like you would get in some
magazines for a garage, shed or
house? The houses here are
timber-framed or steel.

The other program I would like
is to draw airplanes. I know
it's only 48K (the Speccy)but if
I can get a program to do
circuit boards I thought,why not
the other.

One last question if it's OK
with you! What is the address of
Melbourne House? I am trying to
get the understanding of your
Spectrum BASIC and M/Code
programming (ISBN 086161 111x).

          Thanking you

           R. Webster

Brian Cavers to R. Webster

If you have used SAVE SCREEN$ 1
with the Kemsoft program then it
is clear you can enter the BASIC
so try substituting SAVE SCREEN$
2 which gives a bigger dump.

Grant Dixon reviewed Kemsoft's
PCB Designer in OUTLET 19 but it
is not clear if this is the same
program that you have or an
earlier forerunner of it. I know
that Grant uses a Disciple or +D
system and the review seems to
indicate he gets adequate print-
outs. Perhaps Grant can throw
some light on the matter if he
reads this. When you say you got
the program on tape, do you mean
you converted it to +D yourself?

The Kemsoft program Grant rev-
iewed seems to create a design
four Spectrum screens in size so
surely it must have its own
special print routine. A normal
SAVE SCREEN$ will surely only
save a quarter of the image?

Sorry I can't help more on that
particular problem but I don't
have the program or any more
info; in fact you don't actually
name what program you are using!

Ah! Looking at your letter again
I see you mention thirty quid so
it looks to me like it is the
same program as reviewed.In that
case is there a separate program
called "PRINTER"? Surely it must
be designed for the Disciple/+D
printer port?

I don't understand this.You must
have set up your dos correctly
to use a printer in the first
place or else you would not get
anything to print and clearly
you have.

You say in your letter the Kem-
soft program was bought for "my
other interface". Does that have
controlling syntax in the BASIC
and can you not change it to the
+D POKE @6,1?

Tasword 2 is easy to convert to
Disciple/+D. You simply alter
the BASIC load and save syntax
which you must have done anyway
and put the POKE @ you already
have and save the BASIC and code
on disc - no need to snapshot.

If the sort program doesn't work
then double-check your typing,it
may have an error. Mind you,
printed listings are notorious
for the risk of errors therein
which is why it's best to use a
disc magazine like OUTLET! All
our programs work perfectly all
the time. (Ahem!).

One of the problems with solving
readers' questions is that often
not enough information is given
and, of course,this is more true
of learners and beginners who
are the very ones needing help
more frequently.You say there is
a "sort" program in FORMAT that
"will not work" but don't say
which program,which page or what
the symptoms are.

I searched through the February
issue of FORMAT and my guess is
you may mean the routine on Page
7 in SHORT SPOT that reforms a
Tasword file into three columns.
If so, I tried it and it worked
as described although there is
one typing error: STEP 64Z must
be STEP 64: else you won't be
able to enter the line.Also take
care that you use the variable I
(for Initial) and don't read it
as a 1 or an l and also the bit
that says LET I=I+1 must not be
put in as LET I=I+I (I and l are
frequently used by programmers
and yet most likely to confuse).
Check your typing carefully and
let me know if you still get
problems and what exactly you DO
get!

Regarding a program to help you
draw buildings,I thought I heard
that the Kemsoft program could
do more than just design PCB's.
The only one I can offer is
BUILDING (OUTLET 22).This is not
an 'advanced' design program; it
does have features for designing
simple building facades etc. but
is more for enjoyment rather
than serious work. FURNISHER in
OUTLET 11 is also good fun for
designing interior room layouts.

I believe Melbourne House are no
longer trading. The main source
of Spectrum books is now in
small "back-street" bookshops
with old stock - or second-hand
bookshops - or in a library or
in classified adverts for second
hand Spectrum stuff.

If you get Spectrum magazines in
Oz,try reading say,YOUR SINCLAIR
readers' adverts or our own OUT-
BOARD. Why not put a free advert
in yourself?

                          Brian

From: C.Grant Dixon, ROSS-ON-WYE

I was very interested in the
POINTER program in the last
OUTLET. I found there was an
error in the listing as a label
GOTBAR was mentioned but it did
not appear in the listing. After
a little bit of detective work I
found that line 02830 should
read:-
      02830 GOTBAR EX AF,AF'
I thought that it was not too
clear how one was to put in the
data for the arrows, so I wrote
the enclosed program which
prints out the binary patterns
for each pair of bytes. I have
substituted "." for "0" in the
printout in the interest of
clarity. I hope this might be of
interest.

  1 REM This program decodes the
    arrow and mask data files in
  POINT.OBJ and prints them out.
  2 REM It is a useful routine
    to print out a decimal
    number in binary if it is
    suitably modified.
  3 REM Grant Dixon..26.2.92

 10 FOR n=65049 TO 65304 STEP 2
    (2 bytes wide)
 20 LET q=PEEK n:LET p=PEEK(n+1)
 30 LET a=p+256*q
 40 LEt z$=""
 45 POKE @6,1: REM ..needed for
    Disciple interface
 47 LPRINT CHR$ 27;"3";CHR$ 24:
    REM ..altered line spacing
 50 FOR w=1 TO 16
 60 LET b=INT (a/2)
 70 LET c=a-b*2: LET y$"STR$ (c)

 75 IF y$="0" THEN LET y$="."
 80 LET z$=y$+z$
 90 LET a=b
100 NEXT w
110 LPRINT z$;CHR$ 10
120 NEXT n
130 POKE @6,0: REM ..needed for
    Disciple interface
230 STOP

To use the program, CLEAR 54499,
LOAD "POINT.OBJ" from OUTLET 54
then LOAD this program and RUN.

             Yours,

              Grant

Brian Cavers to Grant Dixon

Many thanks. We've typed this in
and checked it as carefully as
possible but readers are warned
that listings are notoriously
subject to typing errors and it
is best to send the program (and
this also saves everybody else
having to type it in!).

Nevertheless, most welcome.

By the way, Grant, if you have
read R. Webster's OUTLETTER this
month about dumps from the KEM-
SOFT PCB DESIGNER program I'd
be grateful for your comments!

                          Brian

From: S. Glenn, COVENTRY

Dear Ron,

I have a problem that I have
been unable to fully resolve. In
previous OUTLETS there have been
two sector-to-sector copy
programs, DBACKER (OUTLET 31)
and SECOP (OUTLET 42). I have
found that when using both of
these programs they have stopped
with disc sector errors.

This was first discovered with
DBACKER when suspecting a faulty
disc I proceeded to try two or
three different discs all with
the same result:-

     3:2,SECTOR ERROR,8O:3.

All discs were then re-formatted
without any problem. Reading and
writing to the faulty sector
using Load @ and Save @ also
proved OK.

Again trying the program on
one of these discs gave the same
result and when continuing the
program (GO TO 81) it eventually
stopped again:-

    18:2,SECTOR ERROR,80:3
GOTO 81
    33:2,SECTOR ERROR,80:3.

The only other thing I could
think of to suspect then was the
drive stepping rate which is set
to 8mS as recommended in the +D
manual.

Taking a large step on the idea
of working backwards I tried
50mS but the problem still
occurred so I decided to go for
broke and try 255mS. To my
surprise the program ran through
perfectly,except that it took
twice as long to get there.

I still run the drive at 8mS for
everything else and in saving
hundreds of programs have only
had half a dozen slightly
corrupted programs which when
resaved were perfect. The discs
in question which gave the
sector errors have all since
been used without any problems.

The SECOP program stops with:-

   28:2,SECTOR ERROR,1025:1

and also works at 255mS stepping
rate. I use one 3.5" drive
(unknown make) purchased with +D
interface from DATEL.

Another problem I have concerns
the printer, CITIZEN 120D, when
printing out from CATLOADER. On
both types of printout if the
printer is fed with a single
sheet and is near to the end,the
paper out sensor doesn't operate
and if the paper runs out the
printer stays on-line and keeps
printing.
                S. Glenn

P.S. Any idea where I can obtain
twin 3.5" drives or how a single
drive can be changed to answer
to drive 2?

Brian Cavers to S. Glenn


The copier programs are O.K. so
it looks like some oddity of the
drive or perhaps incompatibility
with the +D or DOS. It's strange
that in all four examples you
gave it was Sector 2 that gave
the error yet the track always
varied! You say you reformatted
and then could read and write to
the faulty sectors. What you
should have tried was reading
and writing BEFORE you reform-
atted to see if the sectors were
really corrupted

There are two types of sector
corruption:physical and magnetic
thus...

A physical disc corruption means
there is some permanent physical
blemish on the surface of the
disc affecting the ability of
the disc to magnetise correctly
in the area of the blemish. If
this area is large it will
always cause problems no matter
how often you reformat the disc.
The disc might still be used for
some special application - say
to store some permanent files
where you would not need to save
to the disc again. If the files
on the disc are not using the
faulty area there is no problem
but it's best to mark the label
"BAD DISC" or such like so you
don't forget.Another possibility
here is to save lots of dummy
files until one fails and erase
the rest!

The dummy file will remain to
cover the bad area and prevent
anything else being saved there.
The dummy wants naming "BADSECT"
or some such name and must never
be erased.

If the physical blemish is small
it may be avoided by re-formatt-
ing the disc until the fault
happens to fall in the unused
areas BETWEEN sectors. The disc
then acts perfectly but it's
best to mark the disc label else
you may forget and reformat it
later - resurrecting the fault!

The other type of disc corrupt-
ion is magnetic and is due to a
write error or magnetic field
corrupting sector data or the
header.

A magnetic corruption can be
corrected by reformatting where-
upon the disc becomes as good as
new again. Naturally, one copies
what files one can to another
disc first!

All this is just general info.In
your case it seems unlikely that
Sector 2 would always keep being
corrupted coincidentally! I just
cannot think what might cause
this. If it were the same track
each time I would suspect the
drive may have a fault on the
worm screw at the point where
that track was - but the sector
may be anywhere on the track I
believe, depending on the disc
position when the format starts
- which is just chance.

The only suggestion I can think
of that we have sometimes found
SAVE @ fails if the motor is not
up to speed in time or the drive
recording head has not properly
reached the sector. You could
try including a LOAD @ just
before the SAVE @ which may cure
this. SECOP will be easiest one
to alter. BREAK in and add a new
line...
    1024 LOAD @ D2,T,S,16384

This is just before the SAVE @
line at 1025. Note it must NOT
load to address A which would
overwrite the data! Any free
address will do. 16384 is the
top of the screen which will be
corrupted but ignore it. You may
find a better address to use.

Just to clarify, this extra LOAD
@ is a dummy - the data it loads
(in this example into screen
memory) is discarded -it is only
used(hopefully) to get the drive
motor spinning at speed and the
recording head moved to the
right track before attempting
the SAVE @.It will slow down the
whole routine slightly but not
as much as increasing the step
rate to 255! Let me know how you
get on. Any other readers' ideas
would be welcome!

The CATLOADER problem is wierd!
I included a code to stop the
end of paper detector! I cannot
think why I did this. Perhaps it
was something else that became
mistyped. There is an answer...

To correct the paper running out
on the Disciple/+D version of
CATLOADER when using single
sheet paper, remove E$;"8" from
lines 265 and 300. Needless to
say, I use continuous paper so
this does not arise when I use
it. There is a possibility I put
it in for a good reason but I
can't think what!

Now and again we get asked where
readers can buy drives. Usually
I suggest they browse the PC
magazine adverts for an external
(not internal) 720K (gives 780K
on +D) drive. Double-drives are
less common. We got ours through
a trade contact but it took
months and we weren't happy with
what we eventually got, so...

I'd like some feed-back from
readers on where they obtained
their drive(s) for their Plus D
or Disciple. This only applies
to purchases of SEPARATE drives,
i.e.,not bought WITH the +D such
as from Datel. Can the company
be recommended? Do they still
provide the drives? Is a cable
supplied and where there any
problems setting it up? I'd be
particularly interested to hear
from anyone who bought a double
drive system.

I don't believe there's any way
to get a single drive to work
with a d2 command if that's what
you mean. Why would you want to
do that?
                        - Brian

From: Dominic Morris, WORCS.

Dear Brian and Ron,

If possible could you send me a
print-out of the M3UNLOCK in
Issue 40, thanks.

Whilst tabloid printing Output -
the second part of converting
games to +3 disc (it seems a bit
irrelevent to me being as so
many games these days are speed-
locked - one of the main reasons
for my purchasing a Multiface)
and most of the others are
fairly easy to convert, except
for the ones which start at
16384 and length 49152....aargh!
Any suggestions on how to do
these except by using a Multi-
face?)

Now where was I before I launch-
ed into parenthesis?...In, I
think, Issue No.51, the tabloid
print got about 1/6 of the way
through then stopped with an
"invalid colour" error. Have you
got an explanation or even
better a fix? (All my other tab-
loids print out O.K.)

Keep up the good work OUTLET (I
presume you're planning some-
thing for April or is it June? I
can never remember which it is!)

[Well,yes and no but then it all
depends doesn't it if you see
what I mean. Have you taken that
into account? If you think about
it there could be a possibility,
if you follow? Your grass is as
good as mine. - B.C.]

Using the routine on page 201 of
the +3 manual, I'd like to cat-
alogue the drive directly into
part of an array f$(3,64,13) but
I don't know how to find the
address of each part of the
array.

How do you load disc files,
BASIC, CODE, etc. from machine
code?

                 Dominic Morris.

Brian Cavers to Dominic Morris

Sorry,we can't send you extracts
from OUTLET - you need to order
the issue.

The OUTPUT tabloid printing bug
was answered in reply to Phil
Parnell in Issue 54 (although he
has still not confirmed he has
used it).

Programs which are saved as one
long block of code from 16384 to
the end of memory are tough to
transfer to disc. If I were to
tackle it I would first clear
RAMTOP down low and load the
code to say 36384. It would load
but the top part above 65535
would load harmlessly into ROM
at address 0.

You could then peek the code and
examine the BASIC and system
variables (subtract 20000 to get
the true address). By poking the
system variables which lock you
out and possibly altering the
BASIC or redirecting it to a
STOP line you should render it
harmless. Save a temporary copy
on disc as CODE 36384,29152 then
Save it to tape as "x" CODE
36384,29152 and load it back
with LOAD "X" CODE 16384. If you
still can't get in, load the
temporary code back from disc
and search further.

If you get in then save the
BASIC to disc (non-auto run) and
the code above RAMTOP. Now, what
about the top bit of code?...

To get at the top bit of code I
would clear RAMTOP TO about
30000 and load the original code
to about 39680. The top would
wrap around again into the ROM
but the very top bit would reach
to screen memory again from
where you can save it to disc.
You can then match it up with
the other half.

I'm sure that lot won't be very
clear to a beginner but I think
you should grasp it and a
beginner shouldn't attempt it!

I have a routine to find any
variable address but it is a bit
too long to go here.The easy way
is to make your string array the
very first variable declared...

If in doubt, use CLEAR first and
then say, DIM C$(99,10). The
address of the first element of
C$ will be at...

  PEEK 23627+256* PEEK 23628+8

      or in machine code...

  LD  HL,(23627);start of VARS
  LD  DE,8      ;add 8 bytes of
  ADD HL,DE     ;$ array header

For each part of the array of
course, you just add 10 for each
element, e.g., add 490 to get at
C$(50).

Loading files from disc using
machine code is more complex and
of limited use...

Over the years we have seen many
programs produced that access a
particular disc system directly
from code instead of simply
returning to BASIC. They cannot
therefore be converted easily to
other systems and so the market
is unneccesarily restricted. I
would probably not accept any
program for OUTLET that worked
that way unless there was some
special reason.

If you are really determined I
could ask Chris Pile if he might
do an OUTCLASS on the subject
but I would urge you to think
carefully why you want to do it
when BASIC already has the load
and save routines.
                       - Brian

         Burkhard Taige,
    Moorburger Kirchdeich 24
        D-2100 HAMBURG 90

Dear Ron and Brian,

I have a tip for VIDEOFACE users
concerning problems in conjunct-
ion with the DISCIPLE:
Early last year I ordered a
VIDEOFACE from Romantic Robot
UK. It worked fine with my
Speccy's (48K+, Vers. 6A and
128K, Vers. 6U), but with the
VIDEOFACE and DISCIPLE attached
it wasn't possible to use the
disc drive. The drive starts but
runs extremely slowly -it seems
like the power breaks down.

I wrote to RR but haven't had a
reply (a well known problem for
me, after asking MGT, Rockfort
and PBT for spare-parts and
service manual for the DISCIPLE,
who also practiced this kind of
"customer care").


After a lot of experimenting I
found a solution...

With only a few electronic parts
and a switch which have to be
mounted on the VIDEOFACE pcb/
case it is possible to get clear
scanned pictures (without
vertical stripes) onto disc.
With the switch the VIDEOFACE is
now fully compatible with the
DISCIPLE disc interface.

To set up the system, load the
software and make any commands
to the drive(s), e.g., to save
scanned screen$, the switch must
be open (OFF) and the video
camera/recorder must be disconn-
ected.

To scan a picture, the switch is
to set ON (shorten the "-"diode,
make a straight connection to
the Spectrum/DISCiPLE "-" power-
line) and, of course, a video-
source must be connected.


First, I had difficulties with a
50Hz-wave scrolling through the
screen but solved this by fixing
a 220 uF capacitor between the
power-IC Input and ground.

Well it's not a very user-
friendly way to scan pictures
but it is better than to save
the screen$ first on tape.

PRESS THE GRAPHICS KEY NOW
(SHIFT+9) TO DISPLAY A SCHEMATIC
DIAGRAM in which you can see
which parts have to be soldered
into the VIDEOFACE-case.

There is a free place on the pcb
of the VIDEOFACE to place the
power-IC and there is enough
room to place the other parts.

If any OUTLET readers aren't
skilled enough to make this
modification, I think they would
be helped in an electronics
repair shop.

On the other hand, I'll make
this modification to everyone
who sends his VIDEOFACE (+ `10)
for material, work and postage)
to me. If the sender doesn't
forget his address, I'll send it
back as soon as possible.

        Yours sincerely,

            Burkhard

Brian Cavers to Burkhard Taige



Thanks, Burkhard. Er... How come
your English grammar is so much
better than many of the letters
we receive from this country?

                        - Brian

Mr. Vincent L. Jacks, London

I write to ask if you can help
me out with a problem with the
character sets Mini 1 and Mini 2
which are used in my Tasword +2.
I would like to use the sets as
standard character sets in some
of my own programs the problem
being is that although the
character sets are small they
still take up 8 X 8 pixels and
so can only display 32 char-
acters per line. Is there a way
in which I could close up the
spaces between each character
printed - so that I could get
say 64 characters to the line.
Hope you can help. Keep up the
great work.
                 Vincent L Jacks

Brian Cavers to Vincent Jacks

Yes,use HANDYWIDE from OUTLET 7.
This also lets you print in 42
and 51 characters per line as
well as 64. However, it has one
drawback - I had to do a special
version for the +3 so if you
want to use it in any program
for OUTLET I urge you to use a
variable thus.. PRINT #H instead
of LPRINT or PRINT #8 so I can
just alter the value of the
variable when I convert it to +3
(any variable name will do but I
don't fancy going through the
program altering every LPRINT).

[STOP PRESS. We've just got a
NEW 64 column routine to appear
in a couple of issue's time!!!!]
                      - Brian

From: Herman Reichel, GERMANY

Dear Ron and Brian,

I possess the great programs
TASCALC and ART STUDIO 128 for
my Spectrum 128. Unfortunately,
I can't use them with my
Disciple Interface.

Is there for these programs any
convert program? There are these
programs for ART STUDIO 48 and
TASWORD 128.

Best thanks for your effort and
your answer.

             Yours,

         Herman Reichel

Brian Cavers to Hermann Reichel

No, the only conversions I know
of are the ones you mention.

ARTIST II converts easily to the
Disciple/+D because the load and
save is in BASIC but I think the
print routines give trouble. I
don't know how this measures up
to ART STUDIO 128 however. It is
the best graphics program I have
used on the Spectrum.

Regarding an alternative to the
TASCALC program, we hope to have
available soon the best Spectrum
and SAM spreadsheet ever made.It
will run on Disciple/+D. Watch
out for next month's OUTLET!
                        - Brian.

## Letters (2)

M O R E   M A I L ! !

April, 1992      Page Reply

How to write to us...02     - R. Webster...........03    07 C. Grant Dixon.......14    17 S. Glenn.............18    22 Dominic Morris.......30    33 Burkhard Taige.......38    43 Vincent L. Jacks.....44    45 Hermann Reichel......46    47

PLEASE SEND YOUR TEXTFILE! Text is accepted in any form for OUTLETTERS: wordprocessor files (say which),typed or handwritten letters. However, PLEASE send us a textfile if possible so your letter needn't be typed again! The easiest for us to edit are Tasword 2 files with the right margin set at 32 but a textfile in ANY format is appreciated!

Please state if there should be parts of your letter you do not wish published but we always use our discretion anyway. Letters may also be edited for clarity and length... Please ask if you welcome direct correspondence from other OUTLET readers and we will publish your full address.

From: R. Webster, NSW, AUSTRALIA

There are two types of sector corruption:physical and magnetic thus...

A physical disc corruption means there is some permanent physical blemish on the surface of the disc affecting the ability of the disc to magnetise correctly in the area of the blemish. If this area is large it will always cause problems no matter how often you reformat the disc. The disc might still be used for some special application - say to store some permanent files where you would not need to save to the disc again. If the files on the disc are not using the faulty area there is no problem but it's best to mark the label "BAD DISC" or such like so you don't forget.Another possibility here is to save lots of dummy files until one fails and erase the rest!

The dummy file will remain to cover the bad area and prevent anything else being saved there. The dummy wants naming "BADSECT" or some such name and must never be erased.

If the physical blemish is small it may be avoided by re-formatt- ing the disc until the fault happens to fall in the unused areas BETWEEN sectors. The disc then acts perfectly but it's best to mark the disc label else you may forget and reformat it later - resurrecting the fault!

The other type of disc corrupt- ion is magnetic and is due to a write error or magnetic field corrupting sector data or the header.

A magnetic corruption can be corrected by reformatting where- upon the disc becomes as good as new again. Naturally, one copies what files one can to another disc first!

All this is just general info.In your case it seems unlikely that Sector 2 would always keep being corrupted coincidentally! I just cannot think what might cause this. If it were the same track each time I would suspect the drive may have a fault on the worm screw at the point where that track was - but the sector may be anywhere on the track I believe, depending on the disc position when the format starts - which is just chance.

The only suggestion I can think of that we have sometimes found SAVE @ fails if the motor is not up to speed in time or the drive recording head has not properly reached the sector. You could try including a LOAD @ just before the SAVE @ which may cure this. SECOP will be easiest one to alter. BREAK in and add a new line... 1024 LOAD @ D2,T,S,16384

Just to clarify, this extra LOAD @ is a dummy - the data it loads (in this example into screen memory) is discarded -it is only used(hopefully) to get the drive motor spinning at speed and the recording head moved to the right track before attempting the SAVE @.It will slow down the whole routine slightly but not as much as increasing the step rate to 255! Programs which are saved as one long block of code from 16384 to the end of memory are tough to transfer to disc. If I were to tackle it I would first clear RAMTOP down low and load the code to say 36384. It would load but the top part above 65535 would load harmlessly into ROM at address 0.

Существует два типа повреждения секторов: физическое и магнитное...

Физическое повреждение диска означает, что на его поверхности есть постоянный физический дефект, мешающий правильному намагничиванию в этой области. Если область дефекта велика, проблемы будут возникать постоянно, сколько бы вы ни форматировали диск. Такой диск еще можно использовать для каких-то особых задач — скажем, для хранения постоянных файлов, когда повторная запись на диск уже не потребуется. Если файлы на диске не затрагивают поврежденную область, проблем не будет, но на наклейке лучше написать «BAD DISC» или что-то подобное, чтобы не забыть. Еще один вариант — записать кучу фиктивных файлов-пустышек, пока один из них не выдаст ошибку, а остальные стереть!

Файл-пустышка останется, закроет собой сбойную область и не позволит ничего туда записать. Пустышку стоит назвать «BADSECT» или как-то похоже и никогда не удалять.

Если физический дефект невелик, его можно избежать, переформатируя диск до тех пор, пока сбой не попадет в неиспользуемое пространство МЕЖДУ секторами. Тогда диск будет работать идеально, но наклейку все равно лучше пометить, иначе вы забудете и переформатируете его позже — вернув проблему к жизни!

Другой тип повреждения — магнитный, возникающий из-за ошибки записи или магнитного поля, искажающего данные сектора или заголовок.

Магнитное повреждение устраняется переформатированием, после чего диск становится как новенький. Естественно, перед этим нужно скопировать все возможные файлы на другой диск!

После долгих экспериментов я нашел решение...

С помощью всего нескольких радиодеталей и тумблера, установленных на плату/в корпус VIDEOFACE, становится возможным получать на диске четкие оцифрованные изображения (без вертикальных полос). С этим выключателем VIDEOFACE теперь полностью совместим с дисковым интерфейсом DISCIPLE.

Для настройки системы, загрузки ПО и отправки любых команд на дисковод(ы) (например, для сохранения оцифрованного SCREEN$) переключатель должен быть разомкнут (OFF), а видеокамера/видеомагнитофон отключены.

Для оцифровки изображения тумблер переводится в положение ON (закорачивает «-» диод, создавая прямое соединение с линией питания «-» Спектрума/DISCiPLE), и, конечно же, должен быть подключен источник видеосигнала.

Поначалу у меня были проблемы с помехой частотой 50 Гц, плывущей по экрану, но я решил ее, установив конденсатор на 220 мкФ между входом микросхемы стабилизатора питания и землей.

Что ж, способ оцифровки картинок не самый удобный, но все же лучше, чем сначала сохранять экран на кассету.

НАЖМИТЕ КЛАВИШУ GRAPHICS СЕЙЧАС (SHIFT+9), ЧТОБЫ УВИДЕТЬ ПРИНЦИПИАЛЬНУЮ СХЕМУ, где показано, какие именно компоненты нужно впаять в корпус VIDEOFACE.

На печатной плате VIDEOFACE есть свободное место под микросхему питания, и достаточно пространства для размещения остальных компонентов.

Если кому-то из читателей OUTLET не хватает навыков для выполнения этой доработки, думаю, им смогут помочь в любой мастерской по ремонту электроники.
